reviews.author: Illogical Bacon
reviews.text:
The Good:
The location is serene* with easy access to the boat launch and a beachy area with tide pools (we saw starfish!) not to mention you are surrounded by pristine forests and the Chuckanut Mountains with their encompassing trails for both hiking and biking. All of the staff I ran into were extremely pleasant, friendly, and helpful. The bathrooms are some of the cleanest and well-maintained I've encountered at a State Park.

The Bad:
Campsites are close together without much natural barrier between them. Weekends are pretty busy in peak season and you get what you get for fellow camp mates. Getting in and out can sometimes be tricky on the busy road and be VERY cafeful when crossing on foot to access the trailhead across the street.

*The Ugly:
You won't be here for the peace and quiet, as trains run by at all hours of the day and night a mere 500 feet away and there is constant (sometimes obnoxiously loud) traffic noise.

reviews.author: Misha Smith
reviews.text:
Larrabee State Park is definitely one of the few state parks I know I’ll be coming back to. Check-in was super easy, and the staff were very polite, kind, and well-mannered. The park itself is very well maintained, and you can tell the rangers and staff take pride in their work.

Since there was a burn ban during our stay, we brought a propane fire pit, which ended up being perfect—especially when the rain came through. It kept us warm and made sitting outside still enjoyable. Some of the parking stalls are a little close together, but we were able to make it work just fine.

The park has access to a beautiful beach. It’s a bit of a walk to get there, but absolutely worth it. There are also several trailheads nearby, making it a great spot for hiking and exploring. The restrooms were kept very clean and neat, which we really appreciated.

Another plus is the park’s location—it’s close to Bellingham, so if you forget anything, town is just a short drive away.

Overall, this park exceeded my expectations. Huge thanks to the park rangers and everyone who helps maintain such a wonderful place. We’ll definitely be back!

reviews.author: James Airey
reviews.text: Amazing. Peaceful. Beautiful. Affordable. Nice hosts. Glad to be here.

reviews.author: Winston Lai
reviews.text: Campgrounds are nice, but campsites are quite small. Can hear the train and cars pass by but didn’t bother us too much. Firewood available for purchase from camp host for $7/bundle, and beach is quite nice, but you do have to walk from the campsite.

reviews.author: Rob MacMillan
reviews.text: Definitely a nice campground in terms of the layout and ocean lookouts/beach.  That being said, the constant trains made it difficult to get a good night of sleep.  It also sounded like the location was under a flight path and some cars were very noisy.  Great location for popping into town or going mountain biking at Galbraith (definitely a lot of bikers camping).

reviews.author: tjmU4374LJ
reviews.text: It was a short hike to the beautiful water scenery, but before you even get to that part, there are some picnic benches, playground, open green space. Where the path forks, one way gets you to the rocky shore. We had fun going rock to rock and seeing the water and the tide pools in the morning. The tide pools aren't as colorful as the ones we've seen on the Oregon coast, but we could still see some neat aquatic life in them. The other side of the split leads to more overlooks and rocky areas to explore. We had a ton of fun.

Years ago we did a "quick visit" by driving through—missed what us worth seeing here. Recently we had a delightful hour's day hike. First, downhill to large open green area with (historic) large covered kitchens and semi-covered stage. Kids playing in modern playground. A slice of history here. Then, we walked beneath the railroad tracks down to the waterfront. Tidal pools easily located to the right, roughly north, with intricate sculpted sandstone. Kayakers out in force. Fishing on the point. Big views around to the south — out Chuckanut Bay. Train traffic could be loud for overnight stays.

Horrible! Yes trains go by all day & night screeching loud excessive sounds like running right beside the campsite. Can be heard no matter which campsite. The campground hosts never checked on things like 16 people in the site next to us and 6 tents so loud partying noise and music. Max is suppose to be 3 tents and 8 people. Loud noise at 11pm still but no one ever went around checking on things. The beach is small rocky not sand. Not good swimming here.

reviews.author: cohoman
reviews.text: Nice little camp ground and recreational sites. If you like trains one comes through on tracks nearby. Trail to beaches on the Puget Sound. Wetlands. And a wonderful driver back to Bellingham up Chuckanut Dr.

reviews.author: Ben V
reviews.text: Apparently this is the first state park in Washington State. Very nice park that requires a Discover Pass (you can get a one day pass If you don't have one). Several nice bathrooms and play area for kids. Nice trails along the water with great views. They also have lots of hiking trails inland on the opposite side of hwy 11.

reviews.author: Barb L
reviews.text: If I could give 0 stars I would. My family and I arrived at 7 pm (referring to the campground) having been driving down the Al-Can for 5 days and just needed a place to car camp. It is wintertime, so we weren't sure about the restrictions as far as whether the whole campground was even open. The hosts were present and their RV lights were on. We stopped to inquire about the campground and the man and woman inside the RV made eye contact with us through the window, shook their heads, and then proceeded to read their books while ignoring the knocks at the door. This is the last time I try to stay at a State Park due to the absolute rudeness of the hosts. We promptly left as we were made to feel extremely unwelcome. I should also say that I made this account just to leave this review. I don't usually have complaints about places too often, but this was just awful especially after being exhausted after driving to Washington from Alaska in the middle of winter.

Started by walking to the beach which is typical N Washington stony beach. Beautiful walk down and trees right to the beach. Crossed the street from main area and hiked mile up to get to overlook of the bay. Drove through campsites and would like to return to camp. Downside to that is the train which came through twice in the 2 hours we were there.

Tent sites are 31 or 37$ rn. Be aware the sites are very close together state park style. The worst of it is the train tracks are literally right there. Heard no less than 8 trains go by at night over a 12 hour period. You could throw a rock and hit the tracks from some of the sites

Tight busy little city park. All sites are too close and very unlevel. Staff were however very friendly.

Our site T4 was a FHU site, but the sewer cap would not open.

reviews.author: Sherman-Phebes-Winner
reviews.text:
If you pulling a trailer or driving an RV I requested you enter the park from the north ( Bellingham) the road from the south is narrow with lots of sharp curves. The entrance is well marked and the gate attendant was real helpful. Had a pull through site that was on an incline so we used chocks and wheel locks. Sites are narrow so if you have a slide you Neighbor can't have a fire. Toilet and shower building was clean and well lit you had to $$ for the hot showers.

Are kids and grandkids were in site 47-48 and we spent most of our time there. It a short walk to the beach. Good spot for swimming, fishing and crabbing. Watch the tide chart because at high tide there is no beach. On the walk to the beach we found the play equipment and they also have a small amphitheater, and you can reserve the covered picnic area near it. I will go there again.

Did I mention the Train it's loud but didn't hear it in the trailer it is a very busy track!

reviews.author: Iain-and-Tamara
reviews.text: Larrabee State park is a very nice park. This time of year we almost had the place to ourselves. WA state Parks offer free camping with a disabled veteran lifetime pass. The campground is keep clean and tidy. Some of the RV sites are very unlevel. The water is shut off after Nov 1st, but there is winter water available at the restroom. There are train tracks that run right through the park, close to the campground, and the train comes by multiple time throughout the day and night. If you are a light sleeper, it might bother you, but we actually liked it. The park is about 10 minutes south of Fairhaven, and Bellingham proper is 15-25 minutes away depending on where you want to go. The one thing I would give warning about is the south approach to to the park on highway 11. It is a very narrow road and at many points you are driving next to a rocky cliff and the oncoming lane is next to a drop-off, with almost no shoulder. I would recommend coming in from the north.

reviews.author: Love-our-Planet-Adventure
reviews.text: Great place for a 4 things. $40 a night, 20-50 amp hookup. We had a straigh drive thru lot right after Labor Day. 2nd time. Would stay again

reviews.author: camp-roadtripper5256712
reviews.text: We stayed for two nights. The grounds are clean and well maintained. There are lots of hiking trails. We hiked to the beach, only .75 mi from campground. Then hiked Fragrance Lake trail to the lookout point, .9 mi. You could hike extra mile to Fragrance Lake, but we got a late start so we didnt go all the way. The B&N Railroad trains pass by every couple of hours and blow their horns If you are a light sleeper, you might find this annoying. But I liked hearing it and didnt disturb our sleep. We will be back for sure. The beauty of this place looking out to Samish Bay is awesome. 5 stars!

reviews.author: Krista G
reviews.text: Larrabee is such a beautiful accessible park, beach, and boat launch with great views of the San Juan Islands. Wildcat Cove to Dot Island is a nice kayak trip along the sandstone shore with herons and seals to add to the enjoyment.
